text:
Jack Eichel has 27 points in 22 games, 12 of them on the power play, and the way Vegas plays with him on the ice backs most of it up. At five-on-five the Golden Knights get 56% of the expected goals when he's out there (expected goals measure the quality of chances, not just the count), and his 3.64 points per 60 minutes sits near the top of our range for him.

The caution is around him more than in him. Vegas has scored 10.6 more goals than its chances deserve with Eichel on the ice, and on-ice luck like that fades. His last ten games already lean that way: 8 points against the 12.2 our numbers expected.

What shouldn't fade is how he plays. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 11.0 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 98th percentile among forwards, carrying the puck in on 58% of his entries. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 6th of 401 forwards at 3.5 wins above replacement. Watch him at the offensive blue line; that's where his season gets built.
headline: Eichel's points are real, the cushion is not
